content:
District VI voters have a clear choice on the issues closest to home: aging pipes, permits, potholes, parks, and the tax burden. Those were the topics at the center of a debate between the District VI candidates, incumbent Dr. David Tyler King and challenger Ubaldo Granados Jr., according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Water runs through nearly every part of the District VI argument. Laredo's system has faced recurring main breaks, boil-water notices, and long-deferred maintenance, and the debate put the candidates' approaches to fixing pipes and paying for those fixes side by side. Growth is the other pressure point: new development brings new demand on streets, drainage, and services, and voters are weighing who will manage that growth without pushing costs onto existing residents.

The race is one of several Laredo City Council contests on the Nov. 3 ballot, alongside the mayoral race and other district seats. Early voting is already underway in Webb County and runs through Friday, Oct. 30.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “King, Granados debate water, growth in District VI race,” Oct. 2026.

title: District VI debate puts water, growth, and the tax burden front and center
